item.title: Cavan/Monaghan remain 'consistent performers' in IBAL survey
item.description: Cavan and Monaghan have both been described as "consistently good performers" following the latest IBAL survey which was released earlier today. Monaghan has been ranked as the fourth cleanest town in the country. This marks yet another top five position for the county town after it was ranked third cleanest last year. item.title: Man further remanded in jail over fatal Monaghan collision
item.description: A 56-year-old man has been further remanded in jail in relation to a fatal collision in Co Monaghan. Ion Bucurica appeared via video link at Monaghan District Court today charged with dangerous driving causing the death of the mother of two, Emma Mackeral. The Romanian national who resides in France appeared in front of Judge Raymond Finnegan over the alleged offence. item.title: St Brigids to good for Scotstown
item.description: St Brigid's boss Anthony Cunningham says they are delighted to be part of the showpiece event in club football. They booked their spot in the All Ireland Senior Club Football Final after a 1-16 to 1-12 win over Scotstown yesterday (Sunday) in Kingspan Breffni. The Roscommon champions will face Dingle in the decider after falling at the final hurdle two years ago. item.title: Co Cavan pest controller offers winters advice
item.description: A Co Cavan pest control provider is offering advice on how to keep homes pest-free during the winter season. Mark Moore from Ballyjamesduff work for Rentokil, Ireland's leading pest control provider. The Co Cavan man says the most popular creatures that will infest homes in the coming months will be brown rats and house mice. item.title: Over 10% of cars in 2025 at Cavan NCT centre were dangerously defective
item.description: More than one in 10 of all vehicles submitted for an NCT in Cavan last year were deemed dangerously defective. Cavan had a "fail dangerous" rate of 11.4pc during 2025. Other counties with high "fail dangerous" rates include Meath (9.4pc), Clare and Sligo (both 9.2pc) and Monaghan (9.0pc). Advertisement Figures published by the National Car Testing Services show 7.6pc of more than 1.74 million vehicles tested at the country's 50 NCT centres last year were deemed unsafe. item.title: Cavan actress Tina Kellegher on iconic film 'the Snapper'
item.description: Cavan woman Tina Kellegher says starring in the iconic film the Snapper was very enjoyable and she says it was a gift. Tina says she still gets younger people who are only discovering the film now telling her how much they liked it. The low budget film was released 32 years ago and is one of the best-loved Irish films of all times and always a big hit over the festive period. item.title: 'Consistency is key' says Monaghan Tidy Towns
item.description: "Consistency is key" for the Monaghan Tidy Towns Team. Following today's IBAL results, Emer Brennan of Monaghan Tidy Towns says staying in the top five is a "top priority" for the group. Despite retaining its top five position, four of the ten sites surveyed fell short of cleanliness for being moderately littered.
